newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Pretoria cardiologist Wouter Basson, allegedly the founder of a chemical and biological warfare programme for SA, may have some claim to be a victim of a case of mistaken identity after the truth commission said yesterday it had found five defence force members of the same name.

- Local authorities are set to borrow about 800 million rand from the Infrastructure Finance Corporation (Inca) in the next couple of months -- the first major private-sector lending to local government since the political transition.

- The 178 anaesthetists who bought shares in Pulseline, a Medical-controlled company retailing medical products used during anaesthetic procedures, would be informed by the Interim National Medical and Dental Council of SA that they were breaching the council's code of ethics, officials said at the weekend.

- Two acclaimed SA wine critics have raised the ire of local wine farmers by suggesting the infustry benefited from apartheid and by calling for a verification of wine co-operative KWV's assets before it becomes a privately owned company.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The building and construction industry is to receive a 3 billion rand to 5 billion rand boost over the next two to three years with the award of casino licences, Ian Robinson, the executive director of the Building Industries Federation of South Africa, said at the weekend.
- The battered gold price crashed through important support levels on Friday as traders talked of large scale selling from a central bank that could drag the precious metal below $340 an ounce.
- The Competition Board has embarked on a preliminary inquiry into the recently announced 10 percent rise in international air fares from South Africa, said Pierre Brooks, the chairman of the board.

- Doug Ivester, the president of Coco-Cola, is expected to provide details on Monday of a massive investment programme in South Africa that could involve expenditure of as much as one billion rand by the US company and its South African bottlers over the next few years.
SAKE BEELD
- The use of gas is going to play a greater role in South African operations than energy supply, National Utility Service marketing manager Tommy Taylor said.
- Q Data Ltd accelerated its growth in the past six months until last year with good performances from its foreign subsidiaries.
- Iscor Ltd's Saldanha steel plant project is gaining momentum with almost a third of the 6.8 billion rand porject completed.
THE STAR

- Chemical warfare expert Dr Wouter Basson, in police custody on drugs charges, was described last night as the kingpin in the unravelling of third force activities said to involve the former South African Defence Force.
- Four children, aged between four and seven, were burnt to death while playing inside a coal box at a house in Johannesburg's Soweto township on Saturday evening.
